headline: The Toronto Maple Leafs Need More From Depth Players In Wake Of John Tavares' Injury
take:
The Hockey News reports that Toronto center John Tavares suffered a major injury Thursday against Buffalo, and that the Maple Leafs' depth players now have a chance to step up in his absence.

The numbers suggest the drop-off may be smaller than his name implies. So far this season, Tavares has two goals and five assists in seven games, but his 5-on-5 share of expected goals (the quality of chances created versus allowed) is just 29.91%, meaning Toronto has been badly outchanced with him on the ice. The team's share of expected goals is 18.96 percentage points better when he is off it. That is a small sample, but it points to a player who has been a drag on play-driving even as his point total looked fine. His own expected goals of 2.49 sit about half a goal above his two actual goals, so his scoring has not been inflated by luck either.

For the Leafs overall, the concern is larger than one player. Toronto sits at 3-4-2 with a 45.7% expected goal share, and goalie play (2.2 goals saved above expected) is propping up the results. Someone has to drive the play, and so far that has not been Tavares.
